items.actClause: AN ACT to amend the agriculture and markets law, in relation to farm trails, apple trails and cuisine trails
items.memo:
BILL NUMBER:S5720

TITLE OF BILL:

An act to amend the agriculture and markets law, in relation to farm
trails, apple trails and cuisine trails

PURPOSE:

To expand the successful program that established farm trails, apple
trails, and cuisine trails so that they can further economic
development opportunities in our Upstate areas and promote the State's
agricultural, food processing, and tourism industries.

SUMMARY OF PROVISIONS:

Section 1: Amends Agriculture and Markets Law section 284-a(2)(c) to
expand the definition of those products that can be sold, used or
promoted on cuisine trails to include, in addition to wine, other
alcoholic and/or nonalcoholic beverages.

Sections 2 and 3: Amends Agriculture and Markets Law section 284- a(3)
(b) and (c) to expand the number of cuisine trails from 10 to 25 and
farm trails from 10 trails to 25 trails. In addition, it makes it
clear that the Department, if asked to, can use any other descriptive
language or trail name to designate its trail, as long as such name
helps to promote the marketing of such trail's agricultural products,
such as, and purely for example, names such as a beverage, hops, herbs
or fruit trail.

Section 4: Amends Ag. & Markets Law section 284-a (4)so that names,
other than apple, farm or cuisine trails can be used to designate such
a trail as long as it helps to promote the marketing of such trail's
agricultural products.

EXISTING LAW:

Since the law was last amended in 2008, the apple, farm and cuisine
trails programs have been successful and needs to be expanded to
accommodate the heightened state-wide interest in establishing more of
these trails.

JUSTIFICATION:

The experience of the Department of Agriculture and Markets, the
administrator of this agri-tourism program, is that there may be many
more applications for such trails than the number of trails that are
currently authorized under the law. This bill expands the number of
trails. The Department of Agriculture and Markets should have expanded
authority to grant more trail applications so that they can meet the
needs of the trail applicants and their marketing plans.

LEGISLATIVE HISTORY:

New bill.

FISCAL IMPLICATIONS:


None.

LOCAL FISCAL IMPLICATIONS:

None.

EFFECTIVE DATE:

Immediate.
